subject: Private deployment packaging & staggered platform fee + support tiers
messages:
From: Cori Lang <cori@whitecap.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@whitecap.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial packaging for private deployment

SoojIN —

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating Redwood for a multi-site private deployment across three US regions. A couple of asks up front so we can decide whether to proceed to a pilot: 

- Can you share options for handling the platform fee (amortization, milestone credits, or a tiered ramp)?
- We need clarity on operator vs site licensing model and whether operator licenses can be capped for the pilot.
- Support tiers: we need 24/7 coverage for production with an option to upgrade to a named SRE retainer. Can you show pricing deltas?
- Any flexibility on first-year platform fee? Procurement is asking about credits tied to implementation milestones.

I’ve attached our requirements RFP to this thread. Proposed timeline: pilot in July, production by Oct if numbers make sense.

Cori
Cori Lang
Head of Infrastructure, WhiteCap AI
RFP_requirements.pdf (attached)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Cori Lang <cori@whitecap.ai>, procurement@whitecap.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial packaging for private deployment

Hi Cori —

Thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. High level we can do several levers you mentioned; below are options we commonly use for multi-site private deployments. I’ve attached a simple model and an SOW template for discussion.

Option A — Pilot-first: 3-month pilot with a reduced platform fee (50% off month 1–3), capped operator licenses for pilot nodes, then a ramp to full platform fee over 6 months. Pilot includes 20% off the standard SRE retainer if you convert to a 12-month commitment.

Option B — Milestone credits: Full platform fee upfront with 2 milestone credits (implementation completion, production cutover) returned as invoice credits upon verification. Operator licenses priced at a per-GPU seat or an optional site license for large clusters (we recommend site for >10 GPUs per site).

Option C — Staggered amortization: Platform fee amortized across 12 months with a lower effective rate in year 1 if you commit to a multi-year arrangement. Support tier delta: Standard (8x5) -> Premium (24x7) is roughly +30% on the retainer; Named SRE retainer is an additional +60% and includes 1-week dedicated on-call at cutover.

Trade-offs and what we’d need from you to firm numbers: expected average sustained GPU count per site, whether you need air-gapped package/install, and SOC 2 evidence timeline for security review.

Attachments: initial_pricing_model.xlsx, SOW_template_v1.docx

If you’re free I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to run through numbers.

— Soojin
SoojIN Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Cori Lang <cori@whitecap.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, procurement@whitecap.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial packaging for private deployment

Soojin —

Thanks. Pilot-first looks appealing. Two follow-ups from procurement: 

1) Can the pilot have a firm cap on operator licenses (we want to limit spend)?
2) We need the platform fee reduced more aggressively in year one — thinking 40–60% off for months 1–6 rather than just months 1–3.
3) For the Named SRE retainer, is it possible to include a 72-hour SLA for P1 incidents during the pilot and then move to 4-hour during production?

If you can sketch a concrete counter that maps to these asks we’ll review with our CFO and legal next week.

— Cori

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Cori Lang <cori@whitecap.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial packaging for private deployment

Cori —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick reality check and a proposal for trade-offs we can offer: 

1) Operator license cap for pilot: yes — we can cap at the pilot node count and include a 1-month notice to add capacity.

2) Year-one platform fee: we can extend the reduced-rate window to 6 months, but to reach 40–60% off we’d need either a 12-month committed spend or an implementation milestone escrow. Suggested compromise: 45% off months 1–6 with 12-month conversion commitment at the end of the pilot. If you prefer no conversion obligation, we can do 30% off months 1–6 with milestone credits totaling up to 15% of the first-year platform fee.

3) SLA: For pilot we can offer a 72-hour P1 response for named SRE retainer. Production SLA (4-hour P1) is available once you upgrade to production retainer.

We’ll need finance to propose payment schedule options (net-45, milestone payment, or partial upfront). I’ve looped David for finance validation and Marissa for legal on the contract implications.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Reference links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/786545/WP-2026-043

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Cori Lang <cori@whitecap.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial packaging for private deployment — payment / compliance notes

Team / Cori —

From finance side, two-pronged suggestion to make this acceptable to both sides: 

- Payment structure: 30% upfront (covers license provisioning + initial on-prem packaging), 40% on implementation completion (pilot -> production readiness), 30% on final cutover. Net-45 on invoices. If WhiteCap prefers the 45% pilot-discount path, we can convert up to 15% of the final payment into an implementation credit that flows back once production SLA is met for 30 days.

- Compliance evidence: attached SOC2 excerpt; we can provide the full SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. If you need a tighter SOC timeline, we can prioritize audit artifacts for the security review — that may push some deliverables by 2 weeks.

Attachment: SOC2_Excerpt.pdf

If that sounds reasonable I’ll ask legal to prepare a SOW_draft_v2 (with the milestone-credit mechanism) and share a DocuSign ready draft.

— David

From: Cori Lang <cori@whitecap.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial packaging for private deployment — agreement in principle

Thanks all — this is helpful. High-level we can agree in principle to the compromise Ben proposed: 45% off months 1–6 in exchange for a 12-month conversion commitment post-pilot, operator license cap during pilot, and the milestone credit split David outlined.

Next steps for us: please send the revised SOW and a draft contract with the milestone-credit language and a DocuSign route. If possible, include the 72-hour P1 during pilot in the SOW and the production 4-hour P1 once the conversion is confirmed.

We’ll aim to get internal sign-off by the end of next week.

— Cori
Sincerely,
Cori Lang
Head of Infrastructure, WhiteCap AI

Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf
